title: AstraZeneca Taps insitro AI for MASH in Deal Worth Up to $1.5 Billion
content: Advertisement News|Articles|October 15, 2026 AstraZeneca Taps insitro AI for MASH in Deal Worth Up to $1.5 Billion Author(s)Pharmaceutical Executive Editorial Staff AstraZeneca will pay insitro $40 million upfront to apply AI to target discovery in MASH and cardiomyopathies, with no candidates named yet. Advertisement AstraZeneca has signed a drug discovery collaboration and licensing agreement with insitro to apply artificial intelligence (AI) to target identification and therapeutic design in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and cardiomyopathies, the companies announced Oct. 15.1,2 Insitro will receive $40 million upfront and is eligible for up to approximately $1.46 billion in milestones.1,2Sharon Barr, executive vice president and head of BioPharmaceuticals research and development at AstraZeneca, tied the agreement to target selection: “We know that disease biology is incredibly complex, and one of the most critical decisions in R&D is selecting the right target. This strategic collaboration underscores our commitment to maximizing the potential of cutting-edge AI to tackle the root cause of disease. Partnering with insitro, we will use advanced AI to identify the biological drivers of disease to support the rapid discovery of high-quality novel targets, advancing our ambition to deliver the next generation of medicines to patients faster.”1“MASH and cardiomyopathies are prevalent, underdiagnosed diseases where high-content data holds immense potential for uncovering disease drivers. By applying AI to these complex datasets, we can unlock greater discovery power and reveal novel genetic insights.”What are AstraZeneca and insitro agreeing to do?Insitro will use its Virtual Human platform to identify causal disease biology in both indications and advance AstraZeneca-nominated targets from discovery to development candidate.1,2 The platform combines large-scale human and cellular data with AI-enabled target identification and medicine design.1AstraZeneca will take the clinical development and regulatory work and holds exclusive worldwide rights to the selected programs; insitro’s release adds that AstraZeneca will also lead commercialization.1,2Beyond the upfront payment, insitro is eligible for single-digit royalties on global sales.1,2 The two releases describe the milestones slightly differently: AstraZeneca cites development and commercial milestones, while insitro includes discovery milestones.1,2The upfront payment represents less than 3% of the combined headline value, and neither company disclosed the number of targets, program timelines or payment schedule.Why are MASH and cardiomyopathies difficult to treat?Insitro’s release says each disease is defined by heterogeneity, with a single diagnostic label covering patients whose underlying biology differs, which has complicated treatment.2 (()=>{var l=(n,t)=>{let i=async()=>{await(await n())()},e=typeof t.value=="object"?t.value:void 0,s={timeout:e==null?void 0:e.timeout};"requestIdleCallback"in window?window.requestIdleCallback(i,s):setTimeout(i,s.timeout||200)};(self.Astro||(self.Astro={})).idle=l;window.dispatchEvent(new Event("astro:idle"));})(); Daphne Koller, Ph.D., founder and CEO of insitro, said: “MASH and cardiomyopathies are prevalent, underdiagnosed diseases where high-content data holds immense potential for uncovering disease drivers. By applying AI to these complex datasets, we can unlock greater discovery power and reveal novel genetic insights. Our platform simultaneously deconvolutes disease biology and identifies causal drivers of disease pathologies. Partnering with AstraZeneca allows us to pair our deep biological precision with their pharmaceutical expertise and scale with potential for accelerated advancement of novel programs through development and to patients.”2In MASH, the treatment landscape has changed recently. The FDA approved resmetirom (Rezdiffra) in March 2024 under its accelerated approval pathway for adults with noncirrhotic disease and moderate to advanced liver scarring, to be used with diet and exercise. The agency, which at the time referred to the condition as nonalcoholic steatohepatitis, said patients had previously lacked a medication that directly addressed their liver damage, and cited an estimate of 6 million to 8 million U.S. patients at that disease stage.3The cardiomyopathy picture is less defined in the releases, which do not specify which forms are in scope. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, the most common inherited cardiovascular disorder, is estimated to affect 1 in 500 people, and a published review notes that existing studies may have underestimated its prevalence.4 That offers one illustration of the underdiagnosis Koller describes, though it should not be read as the collaboration’s target population.How does the collaboration fit each company’s portfolio?AstraZeneca describes cardiovascular, renal and metabolism as one of its main disease areas and a key growth driver, with an emphasis on the links among the heart, kidneys, liver and pancreas.1 A program spanning a liver disease and heart muscle diseases fits within that framing.Insitro says it has built a multimodal corpus of human and cellular data since 2018 and is advancing nine programs, including genetic regulators of liver fat and fibrosis expected to enter the clinic in early 2027.2 The company reports more than $750 million in capital and existing collaborations with Bristol Myers Squibb, Lilly and Gilead.2 The release does not say how its internal liver programs relate to targets AstraZeneca will nominate.What remains unknown about the collaboration?No candidate, efficacy data or safety data accompany the announcement, and the collaboration sits at the discovery stage. Targets identified through AI-driven analysis of human data will still need validation through preclinical work and clinical trials, where heterogeneity of disease could also affect trial design. Milestone and royalty figures are potential payments contingent on progress that neither company has timed publicly. Neither release addresses market reaction, and independent verification of the platform’s performance in these indications was not available at the time of publication.SourcesAstraZeneca announces new strategic collaboration with insitro to use advanced AI systems to develop transformative therapeutics for difficult to treat cardiometabolic diseases. title: STAT Plus: Coming readout of Kymera eczema trial is a high-stakes moment in a bid to rival Dupixent
content: STAT PlusBiotech Coming readout of Kymera eczema trial is a high-stakes moment in a bid to rival Dupixent Biotech aspires to turn pill into a therapy for multiple immunology and inflammatory disorders Manage alerts for this article Save this story for later Share this article Adobe By Jonathan WosenNov. 2, 2026 West Coast Biotech & Life Sciences Reporter Jonathan Wosen[email protected]Jonathan Wosen is STAT’s West Coast biotech & life sciences reporter. You can reach Jonathan on Signal at jwosen.27. Over the past decade, Sanofi and Regeneron’s Dupixent has become the top-selling drug in immunology, bringing in tens of billions in revenue while transforming outcomes for the 1.4 million patients currently on the therapy for conditions including eczema, asthma, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. But investors and doctors are intensely following an experimental therapy positioned to rival the pharma blockbuster, with results from a key study fast approaching. Massachusetts biotech Kymera Therapeutics plans to announce data from a mid-stage clinical trial of its lead asset, KT-621, in eczema before the end of the year. Market analysts for the investment bank Jefferies, using common shorthand for immunology and inflammatory disorders, have called the upcoming results “one of the most impactful I&I readouts this year.” Advertisement Success (or failure) could have major consequences for Kymera, its growing list of competitors, and the millions of people who live with eczema in the United States. The results could also bolster or dampen the biotech’s aspirations to treat a broader class of immunological diseases with its drug, including chronic spontaneous urticaria and asthma. Analysts forecast that the drug’s sales could reach nearly $4 billion by 2035, including more than $3 billion in eczema revenue, according to Visible Alpha. title: Your Questions Answered: Foundayo’s EU Panel Backing, Enspryng for TED, Gilead’s Masked TCE Bet, FDA’s Rare Disease Overhaul, and More
content: Advertisement News|Articles|October 19, 2026 Your Questions Answered: Foundayo’s EU Panel Backing, Enspryng for TED, Gilead’s Masked TCE Bet, FDA’s Rare Disease Overhaul, and More Foundayo’s EU backing, Enspryng for TED, Gilead’s masked TCE deal, FDA’s rare disease reset, and Bausch + Lomb’s new interim CEO — explained. Advertisement Lilly’s Foundayo Receives Positive CHMP Opinion for EuropeWhat did the EMA committee recommend?The European Medicines Agency’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use recommended granting marketing authorization in the EU for Foundayo (orforglipron) for two indications: weight management in adults with obesity or overweight, and the treatment of type 2 diabetes in adults whose blood glucose is not adequately controlled. The European Commission makes the final approval decision and typically follows CHMP recommendations within a few weeks.What is Foundayo and why does it matter?Foundayo is Eli Lilly’s oral GLP-1 receptor agonist — a once-daily pill that can be taken at any time of day without food and water restrictions. That last point distinguishes it from other oral GLP-1 therapies currently on the market. The drug received FDA approval for obesity in April 2026 and launched commercially in the United States in the second quarter. Lilly has submitted orforglipron for regulatory review in approximately 40 markets globally.The Stories Covered in this PieceEMA Panel Backs Lilly’s Foundayo for Obesity and Type 2 Diabetes in EuropeFDA Approves Enspryng (Satralizumab) for Thyroid Eye DiseaseAstraZeneca Taps insitro AI for MASH in Deal Worth Up to $1.5 BillionFDA Launches Rare Disease Framework InitiativeVir Biotechnology Enters R&D Collaboration with Gilead for Three Novel PRO-XTEN Dual Masked T-Cell EngagersBausch + Lomb Appoints Thomas Appio as Interim CEOWhat does this mean competitively?If the European Commission approves Foundayo, it would become the second oral GLP-1 available in the EU for weight management, following Novo Nordisk’s Wegovy pill, which received European approval in July for weight management only. In the type 2 diabetes setting, Foundayo would compete with Novo’s Rybelsus brand of oral semaglutide, which has been on the European market since 2020 and has grown into a multi-billion-dollar franchise. The CHMP recommendation opens a new competitive front between Lilly and Novo Nordisk in Europe’s oral GLP-1 market, adding to their existing rivalry in injectable incretin therapies.What did the clinical evidence show?The weight management recommendation is based on two studies involving more than 4,740 adults with obesity or overweight. The type 2 diabetes recommendation is based on four studies involving 3,765 adults compared against placebo, dapagliflozin, and oral semaglutide.FDA Approves Enspryng for Thyroid Eye DiseaseWhat was approved?The FDA approved Enspryng (satralizumab), an interleukin-6 receptor inhibitor developed by Roche, for adults with thyroid eye disease on October 16. Roche describes it as the first subcutaneous therapy for the condition — one that patients or caregivers can administer at home after training from a healthcare provider. It is Enspryng’s second indication; the drug was first approved in 2020 for neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.What did the clinical trials show?The approval rests on two identically designed Phase 3 trials, SatraGO-1 and SatraGO-2, which enrolled 258 adults across 19 countries. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients with active, moderate-to-severe disease who achieved at least a 2 mm reduction in proptosis — eye bulging — at week 24. Results diverged: SatraGO-2 met its endpoint, with 52.9% of Enspryng-treated patients achieving a proptosis response versus 23.4% on placebo, and 60.7% showing reduced double vision versus 25.8%. SatraGO-1 did not reach statistical significance, with researchers attributing the gap to an unexpectedly high placebo response.How does this change the treatment landscape?Two disease-specific therapies were already approved — Tepezza and, more recently, Lumvoa — both administered by intravenous infusion. Enspryng’s subcutaneous, every-four-week maintenance dosing offers a different treatment experience, with the key benefit being reduced logistical burden rather than a demonstrated efficacy advantage over existing options. No head-to-head comparison with approved therapies was conducted.What are the remaining unknowns?Roche did not disclose pricing or launch timing. Long-term data beyond week 24 were not described in available sources. Separately, the FDA has granted priority review to a supplemental Enspryng application for myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease, with a decision expected in January 2027. Insitro will receive $40 million upfront and is eligible for up to approximately $1.46 billion in development and commercial milestones, plus single-digit royalties on global sales.What is insitro’s platform?Insitro’s Virtual Human platform combines large-scale human and cellular data with AI-enabled target identification and medicine design. The company was founded in 2018 and reports more than $750 million in capital raised, with existing collaborations with Bristol Myers Squibb, Lilly and Gilead. It has nine programs in development, including genetic regulators of liver fat and fibrosis expected to enter the clinic in early 2027.Why MASH and cardiomyopathies?Both conditions are characterized by disease heterogeneity — a single diagnostic label covering patients whose underlying biology differs — which has complicated treatment development. In MASH, the FDA approved its first treatment, resmetirom (Rezdiffra), in March 2024, but the condition still lacks therapeutic options for most of the estimated 6 to 8 million US patients with moderate-to-advanced liver scarring. The cardiomyopathy scope was not specified in the announcement.What are the limitations of this deal?No drug candidates were named in the announcement. The collaboration sits at the discovery stage, with targets identified through AI-driven analysis still requiring validation through preclinical and clinical work. The $40 million upfront represents less than 3% of the total headline value, and neither company disclosed timelines for milestone payments.FDA Launches Rare Disease Framework InitiativeWhat is the Rare Disease Framework Initiative?The FDA announced a new effort to redesign how drugs and biologics for rare diseases are developed and reviewed. The initiative, outlined in a white paper released by the agency’s Rare Disease Innovation Hub, aims to build a regulatory framework tailored to the realities of small patient populations — covering clinical development, evidence standards, manufacturing review, and the role of patient voice throughout the process.Why is FDA doing this now?Despite years of regulatory flexibility programs for rare diseases, only approximately 5% of rare conditions currently have an FDA-approved treatment. The agency says that gap reflects the need for a more fundamentally tailored approach rather than incremental adjustments to a framework originally designed for common diseases.What are the specific commitments?The initiative outlines six priority areas: greater clarity and predictability in regulatory decision-making through tailored guidance; embedding the patient voice early and at defined milestones; leveraging external expertise for customized review; building shared institutional knowledge; applying risk-based approaches to manufacturing and pre-approval inspections; and championing innovative statistical approaches in rare disease development.What happens next?The FDA is hosting a public meeting on October 28 at its White Oak campus, facilitated by the Reagan-Udall Foundation, to gather input from patients, disease advocates, industry, and other stakeholders. Additional sector-specific roundtables and requests for information will follow. The detailed framework development — which could include new guidance, regulatory changes, and organizational changes within FDA — will be informed by that input.Gilead and Vir Biotechnology Enter $1.87 Billion Masked T-Cell Engager CollaborationWhat are the two companies agreeing to develop?Vir Biotechnology will discover and optimize three novel PRO-XTEN dual-masked T-cell engager development candidates for Gilead, targeting selected solid tumor-associated antigens. Gilead holds an exclusive license to develop, manufacture and commercialize the resulting therapies. Vir will receive $90 million upfront — including $65 million in cash and a $25 million equity investment at a 30% premium — and is eligible for up to $1.74 billion in additional milestones and tiered royalties.What is the PRO-XTEN masking technology?PRO-XTEN is designed to keep T-cell engagers inactive in circulation until they reach the tumor microenvironment, where tumor-specific proteases cleave the mask and activate the drug’s cancer-killing mechanism. That conditional activation is intended to limit systemic toxicity — one of the primary barriers to TCE use in solid tumors — while extending the drug’s half-life and potentially enabling less frequent dosing.Why does this matter for solid tumor oncology?T-cell engagers have proven highly effective in blood cancers but have faced significant limitations in solid tumors, where toxicity and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment have constrained clinical use. Vir’s PRO-XTEN approach directly targets those barriers. title: FDA Grants Accelerated Approval to INOVIO’s Voceryq for RRP, Reducing Surgical Burden
content: Advertisement News|Articles|November 2, 2026 FDA Grants Accelerated Approval to INOVIO’s Voceryq for RRP, Reducing Surgical Burden Author(s)Nicholas Jacobus FDA grants accelerated approval to INOVIO’s Voceryq for reducing surgery frequency in adults with recurrent respiratory papillomatosis. Advertisement NOVIO announced that FDA has granted accelerated approval for Voceryq (doruxapapogene ralaplasmid and lalikinogene sifuplasmid-gxfd), previously known as INO-3107, to reduce the frequency of surgery in adults with recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP).The indication is approved under the accelerated approval program based on demonstrated complete response, defined as no requirement for surgical intervention in the 12 months after treatment in the efficacy population, with continued approval being contingent on verification of clinical benefit in a confirmatory study.1What does the data show?The approval is supported by data from INOVIO’s RRP-001 study, which evaluated Voceryq in 32 adult patients with RRP who had two or more surgeries in the year prior to treatment.1,2 No additional papilloma surgical excisions were required during the dosing window under the study protocol. 26 Patients required three or more surgeries for papilloma excision in the 12 months before treatment and were included in the efficacy evaluation, with a median of 4.5 surgical excisions in that period.1,2 (()=>{var l=(n,t)=>{let i=async()=>{await(await n())()},e=typeof t.value=="object"?t.value:void 0,s={timeout:e==null?void 0:e.timeout};"requestIdleCallback"in window?window.requestIdleCallback(i,s):setTimeout(i,s.timeout||200)};(self.Astro||(self.Astro={})).idle=l;window.dispatchEvent(new Event("astro:idle"));})(); Related Articles FDA Approves Ilumya for Adults With Active Psoriatic Arthritis FDA Extends Talzenna-Xtandi to Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer FDA Approves Subcutaneous Induction for Skyrizi in Crohn's DiseaseSeven of the 26 efficacy-evaluable patients achieved a complete response, requiring no surgical excision of papillomas after 12 months of follow-up, an outcome the company says is not expected as part of the disease’s untreated natural history.1 All 32 patients completed the study, and the full clinical data was published in Nature Communications and in The Laryngoscope.1Kim McClellan, president of the RRP Foundation, frames the approval as a milestone for patient advocacy in drug development. “This new FDA-approved therapy brings us an important step closer to ensuring every RRP patient has access to a non-surgical treatment option that works for them,” she says. “In reaching this milestone, we have shown that patient voices matter in the drug development process.”What is the safety profile?Voceryq is found to be well tolerated, with the most common adverse reactions, occurring in more than 5% of patients, including injection site reactions, headache, fatigue, hypertension, nausea, and dizziness.1,2 Most treatment-related adverse reactions were grade 1 or 2 and transient, and no grade 4 or 5 common adverse events were reported.INOVIO positions the approval as validation of its DNA medicine platform. “With the approval of Voceryq, we believe our DNA medicine platform has the potential to transform the treatment paradigm for RRP by offering a patient-centric treatment option,” says Jacqueline Shea, PhD, INOVIO’s president and chief executive officer. “Voceryq is designed to deliver what we understand matters most to patients, which is the reduction of the surgical burden caused by RRP. We look forward to delivering Voceryq to the RRP community and believe it has the potential to become a new standard of care for this devastating disease.”Simon Best, MD, associate professor of otolaryngology at Johns Hopkins University and a lead investigator on the RRP-001 study, points to the clinical rationale for moving away from repeated procedures. “The approval of Voceryq is an important step in improving the quality of life for RRP patients as every surgery carries the risk of laryngeal injury,” he says. “I believe it is in the best interest of RRP patients that the standard of care quickly transition away from surgical interventions to immunotherapy after RRP is diagnosed.”What’s next?FDA is requiring INOVIO to submit a draft protocol for the confirmatory study by the end of 2026, with alignment on a final protocol expected by mid-2027.2 Voceryq is approved for use in combination with Cellectra 5PSP, INOVIO’s proprietary DNA medicine delivery device.INOVIO is expecting to make Voceryq available to order and ship within approximately 60 days, with full field deployment anticipated during the first quarter of 2027.1 The company is engaging with Syneos Health to support recruitment and deployment of its medical and commercial field teams. The accelerated-approval pathway means commercial uptake will proceed in parallel with continued data generation, leaving the therapy’s long-term standing contingent on how the confirmatory study results compare with this initial 27% complete-response rate.David Crean, a biotech investor and advisor, told Pharmaceutical Executive that FDA has been layering new mechanisms onto its original PDUFA framework to compress review timelines, including the national priority review voucher program that can shrink review from “10-to-12 months to just one to two.” He adds that FDA is also weighing whether a single Phase III trial should become the default for certain programs, a dynamic that mirrors Voceryq’s own single-study accelerated approval.SourcesINOVIO Announces FDA Accelerated Approval of Voceryq Immunotherapy to Reduce the Frequency of Surgery in Adults with Recurrent Respiratory Papillomatosis (RRP) INOVIO, October 30, 2026, https://ir.inovio.com/news/news-details/2026/INOVIO-Announces-FDA-Accelerated-Approval-of-VOCERYQ-an-Immunotherapy-to-Reduce-the-Frequency-of-Surgery-in-Adults-with-Recurrent-Respiratory-Papillomatosis-RRP/default.aspxFDA Approves First Plasmid DNA-based Immunotherapy for Adults with Recurrent Respiratory Papillomatosis Food and Drug Administration, October 30, 2026, https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-plasmid-dna-based-immunotherapy-adults-recurrent-respiratory-papillomatosis Newsletter Lead with insight with the Pharmaceutical Executive newsletter, featuring strategic analysis, leadership trends, and market intelligence for biopharma decision-makers. After months of anticipation, the Food and Drug Administration gave tentative approval to Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories to make a generic version of a groundbreaking HIV prevention medicine, a key step in widening access for dozens of low- and middle-income countries. title: Genmab soars to record highs after cancer drug succeeds in key trial
content: An article from Dive Brief Genmab soars to record highs after cancer drug succeeds in key trial The latest data adds to a streak of readouts that could position the company to surpass $10 billion in total annual revenue in the years ahead, according to analysts. At an early analysis, a combination of Genmab’s drug petosemtamab and the immunotherapy Keytruda, cut the risk of death by half compared to Keytruda alone when used as a first-line treatment in people whose head and neck squamous cell carcinoma is positive for the protein PD-L1. The regimen met dual main objectives on response rates and survival. The latest finding represents the third consecutive positive late-stage readout in a few weeks for Genmab, providing an important boost ahead of the patent expiry for the multiple myeloma drug Darzalex. The drug — a bispecific antibody targeting the proteins EGFR and LGR5 — had already produced positive results in a Phase 2 trial. Genmab predicted the antibody could become a blockbuster by 2029, should those results be replicated in a late-stage study. Ahead of those findings, Genmab scored two other wins that have lifted its revenue potential. Earlier this month, the company and partner AbbVie announced the blood cancer drug Epkinly succeeded in a Phase 3 trial in frontline lymphoma. Wall Street analysts claimed the results have positioned Epkinly to become a new treatment standard in people with newly diagnosed, diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. The company continued its streak last week when an antibody-drug conjugate dubbed rinatabart sesutecan hit its goal in a late-stage study in ovarian cancer. Wednesday’s result positions petosemtamab to become part of a new treatment standard in first-line head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, wrote TD Cowen analyst Yaron Werber. The findings should support a “broad” label enabling access regardless of whether patients’ tumors are driven by HPV infections, he wrote. The trio of successes show Genmab has “delivered on the late-stage catalysts that define the company’s longer-term growth story,” wrote William Blair analyst Matt Phipps, in a Thursday client note. The company is now on the path to surpassing $10 billion in annual revenue, with pending launches that can “more than offset the impending loss of Darzalex royalties,” Phipps added. Petosemtamab is being tested in multiple other Phase 3 trials, among them studies in second- and third-line recurrent head and neck cancer, and a trial in colorectal cancer. 10月29日，Incyte公布2026年第三季度业绩，旗下芦可替尼乳膏（Opzelura）继续保持增长。图源：Incyte企业第三季度财报公告财报显示，Opzelura第三季度净销售额达2.55亿美元，同比增长36%；前三季度累计净销售额达8.48亿美元。Incyte将全年销售预期再次上调至11.00亿—11.20亿美元，这是年内第二次上调。全球销售持续增长的同时，Opzelura也在拓展新的适应症。国内市场方面，康哲药业引进的产品已获批上市，后续适应症布局同样值得关注。一、全球销售持续增长，第3个适应症进入关键阶段作为全球首款获批上市的外用JAK抑制剂，Opzelura目前已在海外获批用于白癜风和特应性皮炎。2026年7月，欧盟批准其用于成人中度特应性皮炎，进一步拓展了产品的适用范围。在已有适应症之外，Opzelura正在探索新的治疗领域——化脓性汗腺炎（HS）。图源：Incyte企业第三季度财报公告目前，Incyte正在开展两项Ⅲ期研究TRuE-HS1和TRuE-HS2，预计于2026年第四季度公布总体结果。如果研究结果积极，Opzelura有望进一步拓展适应症范围，打开新的市场空间。二、国内首款白癜风靶向药，上市后销量迅速攀升芦可替尼乳膏最初由Incyte开发。2021年，该产品在美国获批上市，成为首个在美国获批的外用JAK抑制剂。2022年，康哲药业旗下子公司德镁医药与Incyte达成合作，获得芦可替尼乳膏在中国及东南亚地区的独家研发、注册及商业化权利。2026年1月30日，康哲药业宣布，旗下德镁医药磷酸芦可替尼乳膏新药获国家药监局批准上市，用于12岁及以上儿童和成人面部受累的非节段型白癜风患者，成为国内首款获批用于白癜风治疗的靶向药物。图源：摩熵医药-中国药品审评数据库2026年3月，磷酸芦可替尼乳膏在京东健康上市当天销量突破5000+，上市近15天累计销量突破1万+。作为国内首款白癜风外用JAK抑制剂，该产品售价为5800元/支，尽管价格不低，上市初期仍表现出较高的市场热度。临床疗效方面，TRuE-V1和TRuE-V2研究显示，治疗第24周，芦可替尼乳膏组F-VASI75应答率均为29.9%，安慰剂组分别为7.5%和12.9%。此外，康哲药业正推进芦可替尼乳膏在特应性皮炎领域的适应症拓展。Ⅲ期研究显示，治疗第8周，芦可替尼乳膏组IGA title: 恒瑞医药三季报炸场：归母净利暴增88.92%，创新药持续增长，ADC瑞康曲妥珠单抗第5项适应症获受理
content: 首页 资讯 摩熵原创 时讯 恒瑞医药三季报炸场：归母净利暴增88.92%，创新药持续增长，ADC瑞康曲妥珠单抗第5项适应症获受理 恒瑞医药三季报炸场：归母净利暴增88.92%，创新药持续增长，ADC瑞康曲妥珠单抗第5项适应症获受理 李明轩 · 医药投融资分析师 李 李明轩 医药投融资分析师 审核：孙浩 · 特许金融分析师（CFA） 聚焦创新药投融资、小核酸药物与代谢疾病赛道；长期跟踪国内 Biotech 融资动态与管线进展。累计发布原创分析 200+ 篇。 2026/10/29 4714 GIP GLP-1 江苏恒瑞医药股份有限公司 瑞康曲妥珠单抗 HER2 10月28日，恒瑞医药发布2026年第三季度报告。第三季度，公司实现营业收入89.53亿元，同比增长20.55%；归母净利润24.58亿元，同比增长88.92%；利润总额27.76亿元，同比增长103.97%。前三季度，公司实现营业收入244.09亿元，归母净利润69.23亿元，同比增长20.38%。图源：恒瑞医药2026年第三季度报告业绩增长的同时，恒瑞医药创新药业务也有新进展。CDE官网同日公示，公司自主研发的ADC药物瑞康曲妥珠单抗一项新适应症上市申请获受理。结合该药此前的临床研究及审评进展，此次申报可能涉及HER2阳性复发或转移性乳腺癌一线治疗，具体适应症仍需以官方披露为准。一、创新药销售超138亿元，对外授权持续贡献收入从前三季度经营情况来看，创新药已成为恒瑞医药收入的重要组成部分。2026年前三季度，公司创新药销售收入达138.71亿元，同比增长17.05%，占药品销售收入的比重提升至64.59%。其中，抗肿瘤创新产品收入98.65亿元，同比增长3.13%，占创新药销售收入的71.12%；非肿瘤创新产品收入40.06亿元，同比增长75.36%，占比达到28.88%。图源：整合于恒瑞医药2026年第三季度报告除产品销售外，创新药对外许可业务也为公司带来收入增量。前三季度，恒瑞医药创新药对外许可业务确认收入27.81亿元，同比增长31.12%，主要来自GSK、BMS相关合作的进度确认收入，以及个别已授权产品的里程碑款。同期，公司收到对外许可合作首付款及里程碑款现金共43.43亿元，主要包括BMS支付的6亿美元首付款。第三季度单季确认许可收入约13.6亿元，这类收入具有较高毛利率。在已授权项目持续贡献收入的同时，恒瑞医药也在拓展新的海外合作。2026年9月，公司与诺和诺德达成协议，将每周一次口服给药的GLP-1/GIP双受体激动剂HRS-1596有偿许可给诺和诺德，授予其大中华地区以外全球范围内的开发、生产和商业化独家权利。该交易潜在总金额最高可达26亿美元，包括3亿美元首付款，以及后续开发、注册和商业化里程碑付款及销售提成。另一条出海路径是NewCo模式。8月6日，恒瑞医药的合作伙伴Braveheart Bio登陆美国纳斯达克。此前，恒瑞将自主研发的心肌肌球蛋白小分子抑制剂HRS-1893有偿许可给Braveheart Bio，并获得该公司部分股权。这是继今年4月Kailera Therapeutics登陆纳斯达克后，恒瑞医药NewCo模式取得的又一进展。二、多款创新药上市申请获受理，研发管线持续推进销售与授权业务之外，创新药研发及上市申报进展同样值得关注。2026年第三季度，恒瑞医药共有7项上市申请获CDE受理，其中GLP-1相关产品取得多项进展。企业公告+摩熵医药全球药物研发数据库整合具体来看，口服GLP-1受体激动剂HRS-7535片用于成人2型糖尿病患者血糖控制、成人长期体重管理的两项上市申请均获受理；GLP-1/GIP双受体激动剂瑞普泊肽注射液用于成人2型糖尿病患者血糖控制的上市申请也获受理。从产品储备来看，截至目前，恒瑞医药已有27款1类创新药和6款2类新药在中国获批上市，另有100多个自主创新产品处于临床开发阶段，400余项临床试验在国内外开展。多款产品推进上市申报，也为公司后续创新药商业化提供了新的观察窗口。 title: FDA Approves Ilumya for Adults With Active Psoriatic Arthritis
content: Advertisement News|Articles|October 30, 2026 FDA Approves Ilumya for Adults With Active Psoriatic Arthritis Author(s)Pharmaceutical Executive Editorial Staff Sun Pharma's IL-23 inhibitor tildrakizumab gains a psoriatic arthritis indication; the announcement cited no phase 3 efficacy figures. Advertisement FDA has approved Sun Pharma’s Ilumya (tildrakizumab-asmn) for adults with active psoriatic arthritis, the company announced Oct. 30.1 The decision adds a second disease to the label of the interleukin-23 (IL-23) inhibitor, which FDA first approved in 2018 for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. The expansion extends the product from dermatology into rheumatology, where Sun Pharma estimates that as many as 2.4 million Americans live with the disease.1“FDA approval of Ilumya for adults with active psoriatic arthritis represents another important innovative medicine milestone for Sun Pharma and builds on the established clinical experience of Ilumya in plaque psoriasis,” said Rick Ascroft, North America CEO, Sun Pharma. “As an IL-23 inhibitor administered exclusively by a healthcare provider, Ilumya is now an option for adults with active psoriatic arthritis who are unable to self-administer treatment or who may benefit from regular in-office care.”1Key FactsDrug: Ilumya (tildrakizumab-asmn), IL-23 inhibitorIndication: Adults with active psoriatic arthritisTrials: Phase 3 INSPIRE-1 and INSPIRE-2Efficacy: ACR20 endpoint met at week 24 (no rates)Safety: No new signals reported by companyStatus: FDA-approved; U.S.; clinician-administeredSun Pharma is positioning provider administration as the product’s distinguishing feature. The announcement did not address launch timing, pricing or how payers might view an in-office model. Ilumya is also approved for plaque psoriasis in India, Australia, Canada, China and Japan, and in Europe as Ilumetri, which Almirall markets.1What data support the approval?The approval rests on two phase 3 studies, INSPIRE-1 and INSPIRE-2, which compared Ilumya 100 mg with placebo over 52 weeks in adults with active psoriatic arthritis.1 INSPIRE-1 enrolled patients with prior exposure to a tumor necrosis factor (TNF) inhibitor and INSPIRE-2 enrolled patients without it; together they included more than 800 participants. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients achieving at least a 20% improvement in American College of Rheumatology response criteria (ACR20) at week 24, and the company reported in 2025 that both studies met it.2 The announcement did not include ACR20 response rates. Sun Pharma said the studies identified no new safety signals and that safety was consistent with the drug’s established profile. Upper respiratory tract infections were among the most common adverse reactions in the arthritis studies, and patients should be evaluated for tuberculosis before treatment begins.1 (()=>{var l=(n,t)=>{let i=async()=>{await(await n())()},e=typeof t.value=="object"?t.value:void 0,s={timeout:e==null?void 0:e.timeout};"requestIdleCallback"in window?window.requestIdleCallback(i,s):setTimeout(i,s.timeout||200)};(self.Astro||(self.Astro={})).idle=l;window.dispatchEvent(new Event("astro:idle"));})(); How does it fit the psoriatic arthritis treatment landscape?Psoriatic arthritis can cause joint pain, swelling and stiffness that may lead to permanent joint damage, and roughly one in three people with psoriasis also have it, according to the company. Sun Pharma adds that more than 15% of people with psoriasis may have undiagnosed psoriatic arthritis.1 Treatment options already include biologic drugs that target TNF and targeted synthetic agents.3“Psoriatic arthritis is a complex and chronic disease. As clinicians, we need a range of therapeutic options that allow us to individualize care based on each patient’s symptoms and treatment goals. Adding an IL-23 inhibitor option that is administered by a healthcare provider gives us a new way to offer appropriate patients additional support and engagement with their healthcare team,” said Philip Mease, Director of Rheumatology Research at the Swedish Medical Center and Providence St Joseph Health and Clinical Professor at the University of Washington School of Medicine, Seattle, WA.1 Mease was first author of the earlier phase 2b study of tildrakizumab in the condition.3What did earlier studies show?Ilumya’s psoriasis record is longer than its arthritis record. title: Lilly’s ‘triple-G’ drug tops Novo’s Ozempic in diabetes trial
content: An article from Dive Brief // Obesity drugs Lilly’s ‘triple-G’ drug tops Novo’s Ozempic in diabetes trial The highest dose of retatrutide beat Ozempic on measures of blood sugar and weight loss, but was also associated with higher side effect rates and treatment discontinuations. Published Oct. 28, 2026 Jonathan Gardner Senior Reporter Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Boxes of the diabetes drug Ozempic rest on a pharmacy counter on April 17, 2023 in Los Angeles, California. Mario Tama / Getty via Getty Images Dive Brief: Eli Lilly’s triple-acting metabolic drug retatrutide bested Novo’s Ozempic in a head-to-head Phase 3 trial, with the highest dose tested beating Novo’s drug on measures of blood sugar and weight loss, the company said Wednesday. After 80 weeks of treatment, a 12 milligram weekly dose of retatrutide lowered blood sugar by an average of 2.2 percentage points, significantly more than Ozempic’s 1.8 percentage points, Lilly said. A 9 mg dose of retatrutide also lowered blood sugar by 2.2 percentage points, but the difference when compared to Ozempic was statistically “nominal,” the company said. The results confirm earlier findings suggesting retatrutide — which acts on three metabolic pathways versus one for Ozempic — could be a differentiated diabetes and weight loss medicine. The ascent of its already-marketed Zepbound and Mounjaro have propelled Lilly’s market value far beyond that of its pharmaceutical peers. And the buzz surrounding retatrutide is so strong that many people have resorted to a nebulous “black market” to get their hands on it. Retatrutide represents the next step in a push by obesity drug developers to make therapies that can drop weight even more profoundly than existing medications. While GLP-1 medicines have been on the market for more than 20 years, for instance — Lilly was the commercial partner for the first such shot — the company has been specializing in drugs that add more metabolic targets to boost effectiveness. Zepbound and Mounjaro modulate GLP-1 as well as a second hormone called GIP. Retatrutide acts on a third, called glucagon, too. Novo is aiming to catch up, but has yet to launch a dual acting drug, and its three-pronged candidates are in Phase 2 trials. The latest trial result showed just how challenging a foe retatrutide might be for Novo. The highest dose lowered weight by 21% on average, while a 9 mg dose was associated with 20% weight loss. That number was 9% for Ozempic recipients. Those benefits appear to come with a trade-off. In the study, only 3% of Ozempic recipients stopped treatment because of side effects compared with 8% of the people on the highest retatrutide dose and 5% of those in the 9 mg group. Still, the results “strengthen the case for retatrutide’s long-term differentiation” and justify a “branded premium” ahead of the 2032 U.S. patent expiration of semaglutide, wrote Leerink analyst David Risinger in a client note. Risinger expects annual retatrutide sales to reach $15 billion in 2032, higher than the $10 billion consensus among Wall Street analysts. MADRID — A personalized mRNA cancer vaccine reduced the risk of disease recurrence in patients with melanoma by 42% compared to a standard treatment, according to a large clinical trial conducted by the drugmakers Moderna and Merck. The results are an important advance for the treatment of melanoma, oncologists said, because patients lived significantly longer without their cancer returning. title: 步长制药AGT小核酸BC923及PD-1/TIGIT双抗BC008-1A同日获批临床，剑指高血压与复发性脑胶质瘤
content: 首页 资讯 摩熵原创 注册审批 步长制药AGT小核酸BC923及PD-1/TIGIT双抗BC008-1A同日获批临床，剑指高血压与复发性脑胶质瘤 步长制药AGT小核酸BC923及PD-1/TIGIT双抗BC008-1A同日获批临床，剑指高血压与复发性脑胶质瘤 张鹏 · 新药研发分析师 张 张鹏 新药研发分析师 审核：王正晴 · 药学博士 关注全球创新药研发管线、临床试验进展与注册审批动态；重点分析热门靶点、临床价值与管线竞争格局。累计发布研发分析 102+ 篇。 2026/10/30 3364 PD-1 AGT TIGIT 水痘 高血压 10月29日，步长制药发布公告称，公司两家控股子公司同日收到国家药品监督管理局核准签发的《药物临床试验批准通知书》。其中，化学药品1类新药BC923注射液获准开展高血压适应症临床试验；生物制品1类新药BC008-1A注射液获准开展新增适应症临床试验，拟联合贝伐珠单抗治疗成人复发性CNS WHO 4级脑胶质瘤。两款1类新药同步取得临床进展，分别布局高血压和复发性脑胶质瘤，涉及AGT靶向小核酸药物、PD-1/TIGIT双特异性抗体两条技术路线。与此同时，步长制药的独家中成药前列舒通胶囊获得印度尼西亚药品上市许可批准，2025年国内销售额已超6亿元。从创新药研发到成熟品种出海，步长制药的产品布局正呈现出不同的发展路径。一、两款1类新药同日获批临床，分别布局高血压与脑胶质瘤BC923靶向血管紧张素原（AGT）—— 肾素 - 血管紧张素系统（RAS）上游前体蛋白，从源头抑制 AGT 合成、减少血管紧张素生成，为降压治疗提供不同于传统受体 / 酶抑制的新路径。全球范围内，AGT靶向小核酸药物仍处于研发阶段，尚无同靶点产品获批上市。国际研发进展较快的代表之一，是Alnylam开发的zilebesiran。其KARDIA-1、KARDIA-2两项Ⅱ期研究显示，皮下注射后降压效应可维持数月，展现出长间隔给药的潜力。截至2026年9月30日，公司在BC923注射液项目上投入的研发费用约为 3,205.73 万元。zilebesiran临床试验部分数据图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库BC008-1A为重组抗PD-1/TIGIT人源化双特异性抗体，可同时阻断两条免疫抑制信号通路。本次新增适应症拟联合贝伐珠单抗，探索免疫双靶点阻断与抗血管生成联合策略，直指治疗选择有限的复发性高级别脑胶质瘤。该药此前已获批实体瘤适应症临床试验，此次获批属于新增适应症的临床开发进展，并非首次进入临床阶段。截至2026年9月30日，公司在BC008-1A注射液项目上投入的研发费用约为11,668.71万元。二、超6亿大单品出海，国内销售额逐年增长10月21日，步长制药公告称，其全资子公司保定天浩制药生产的前列舒通胶囊获得印度尼西亚药品上市许可。这款国内年销售额超过6亿元的独家中成药，在国内市场持续增长的同时，也迎来了海外市场的新进展。前列舒通胶囊为国家医保乙类药品，功能主治为清热利湿、化瘀散结，适用于慢性前列腺炎、前列腺增生属湿热瘀阻证。据摩熵医药数据库数据显示，近年来，前列舒通胶囊在全终端销售额呈逐年增长趋势，2025年超过6亿元，2026年上半年超过3亿元，同比增长9.01%。从销售表现来看，该产品已形成一定的市场规模，此次获得印尼上市许可，也为其后续海外市场拓展提供了新的契机。 content: 首页 资讯 摩熵原创 注册审批 两款中药新药同日获批！完带汤颗粒国内首家上市，瑞阳制药桃红四物汤颗粒布局妇科经典名方赛道 两款中药新药同日获批！完带汤颗粒国内首家上市，瑞阳制药桃红四物汤颗粒布局妇科经典名方赛道 张鹏 · 新药研发分析师 张 张鹏 新药研发分析师 审核：王正晴 · 药学博士 关注全球创新药研发管线、临床试验进展与注册审批动态；重点分析热门靶点、临床价值与管线竞争格局。累计发布研发分析 102+ 篇。 18小时前 950 四川光大制药有限公司 瑞阳制药股份有限公司 获批上市 桃红四物汤颗粒 完带汤颗粒 经典名方 近期，国家药监局（NMPA）官网显示，四川光大制药申报的中药3.1类新药完带汤颗粒获批上市，成为国内首家获批的同名产品。图源：NMPA官网与此同时，瑞阳制药申报的中药3.1类新药桃红四物汤颗粒也获批上市。两款古代经典名方相继获批，为中药经典名方的开发和产业化再添新进展。一、两款经典名方获批，妇科用药再添新品完带汤颗粒源自清代傅山所著《傅青主女科》，是中医妇科治疗带下病的经典方剂，具有补脾疏肝、化湿止带的功效，主要用于肝郁脾虚、湿浊下注所致的带下病，常见症状包括带下色白或淡黄、质地清稀、倦怠便溏等。图源：摩熵医药-中国药品审评数据库近年来，完带汤在妇科相关疾病的辨证治疗中受到关注。此次四川光大制药申报的完带汤颗粒获批上市，也意味着这一经典名方进一步实现现代剂型转化。另一款获批产品桃红四物汤颗粒，则来自瑞阳制药。该产品属于中药3.1类新药，处方源自清代柴得华《妇科冰鉴》，具有养血活血、化瘀调经的功效，主要用于血虚血瘀所致的妇女月经不调、经血量多有块、色紫质稠、腹痛腹胀等症。桃红四物汤是中医妇科经典方剂之一，在养血活血、化瘀调经方面具有较高的临床应用价值。此次颗粒剂获批上市，也为经典名方的现代化开发提供了新的产品选择。二、瑞阳制药再添经典名方，4款创新药持续推进对于瑞阳制药而言，桃红四物汤颗粒的获批，是其经典名方研发管线的又一项进展。截至目前，瑞阳制药已有两款古代经典名方获批上市。其中，今年7月获批的五味消毒饮颗粒是公司首款中成药皮肤科用药；此次获批的桃红四物汤颗粒，则是公司在中成药妇科用药市场布局的首个古代经典名方。从皮肤科到妇科，瑞阳制药正进一步拓展中成药产品布局。 content: STAT PlusNewsletterPharmalot Pharmalittle: We’re reading about a Roche lung cancer drug, a Bristol CAR-T trial death, and more Most recently approved cancer drugs in Europe do not offer high clinical benefit, analysis finds Manage alerts for this article Save this story for later Share this article Alex Hogan/STAT By Ed SilvermanOct. 26, 2026 Pharmalot Columnist, Senior Writer Ed Silverman[email protected]Ed’s stories explore prescription drug pricing, affordability and access, as well issues surrounding patents, litigation, and legislation. He is also the author of the morning Pharmalittle newsletter and the afternoon Pharmalot newsletter. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to another working week. We hope the weekend respite was relaxing and invigorating because that oh-too-familiar routine of meetings, deadlines, and the like has returned with a vengeance. But what can you do? The world, such as it is, continues to rotate. To nudge it in a better direction, we are brewing another cup of stimulation. Our choice today is butter pecan with a dash of raw honey. Feel free to join us. Remember, no prescription is required. Meanwhile, here are some tidbits to help you along. Best of luck accomplishing your goals today, and of course, do keep in touch. … Bristol Myers Squibb reported that one patient died after receiving its investigational CAR-T therapy in an early autoimmune trial, adding to safety concerns about a growing field of research, STAT notes. In a Phase 1 trial that tested the therapy in multiple sclerosis, the patient experienced motor symptoms that did not resolve with standard autoimmune treatments. They were then given a potent immunosuppressant, but developed septic pneumonia and died, Bristol said in a press release. In a subsequent statement, Bristol said this patient was treated for a series of other complications prior to receiving the CAR-T therapy, “confounding our ability to determine the root cause of the issue.”Advertisement A Roche drug billed as a potential blockbuster helped patients with a form of lung cancer that had spread live almost six months longer than two competitive medicines, Bloomberg News says. The experimental treatment, called divarasib, fared better than similar drugs from Amgen and Bristol Myers Squibb in a late-stage study. The drug was given to patients with non-small cell lung cancer that had spread, in part because of a genetic mutation, after other treatments, including chemotherapy. The findings could help divarasib become the treatment of choice for this type of lung cancer, in which a mutation called KRAS G12C drives the tumor cell growth. content: 首页 资讯 摩熵原创 时讯 诺诚健华Q3营收大增150.60%：BD里程碑收入推高业绩，奥布替尼独挑商业化大梁 诺诚健华Q3营收大增150.60%：BD里程碑收入推高业绩，奥布替尼独挑商业化大梁 李明轩 · 医药投融资分析师 李 李明轩 医药投融资分析师 审核：孙浩 · 特许金融分析师（CFA） 聚焦创新药投融资、小核酸药物与代谢疾病赛道；长期跟踪国内 Biotech 融资动态与管线进展。累计发布原创分析 200+ 篇。 2026/10/29 4720 BTK 佐来曲替尼 坦昔妥单抗 奥布替尼 北京诺诚健华医药科技有限公司 药品销售增速与整体营收增速之间的明显差距，主要来自BD里程碑收入的确认。诺诚健华（688428.SH/09969.HK）第三季度营业收入同比大增150.60%。但同期药品销售收入增速为38.59%。两组数据出现明显剪刀差，内生盈利能力引发市场关注。10月26日，诺诚健华发布2026年第三季度报告显示，前三季度，公司实现营业收入20.99亿元，同比增长88.21%；归属于上市公司股东的净利润6.56亿元，扣除非经常性损益后的净利润为5.86亿元，实现持续盈利；经营活动产生的现金流量净额为2.20亿元，同比由负转正。图源：诺诚健华官网从增长动因看，除奥布替尼持续放量、坦昔妥单抗和佐来曲替尼新增销售贡献外，诺诚健华与Zenas BioPharma（下称“Zenas”）的授权许可合作完成后续里程碑交付，成为营收增长的重要因素。另一方面，公司单品依赖问题仍较为突出。奥布替尼作为公司商业化收入的核心支柱，仍面临激烈竞争。在27日的业绩说明会上，以诺诚健华首席财务官傅欣为代表的部分高管，一方面坦承BD收入成为公司业绩核心助推力量；另一方面也表示，公司正在着手通过坦昔妥单抗、佐来曲替尼等产品强化公司的商业化盈利能力。一、BD里程碑收入助推单季净利扭亏诺诚健华成立于2015年，是一家处于商业化阶段的生物医药高科技公司，专注于恶性肿瘤及自身免疫性疾病领域一类新药的研发。公司于2020年3月在港交所上市，2022年9月登陆上交所科创板，并于2025年首次实现年度盈利。从单季度表现看，诺诚健华2026年第三季度实现营业收入9.62亿元，同比增长150.60%；归母净利润约4.09亿元，同比扭亏。公司在三季报中解释称，营收增长主要来自奥布替尼持续放量、坦昔妥单抗和佐来曲替尼新增销售贡献，以及与Zenas授权许可协议完成后续里程碑交付。不过，进一步拆分收入结构可以看到，公司整体营收增速明显快于药品销售增速。三季报显示，前三季度公司药品销售收入为14.49亿元，同比增长41.47%，而营业收入同比增长88.21%；单季度看，第三季度药品销售收入为5.31亿元，同比增长38.59%，而营业收入同比增长150.60%。药品销售增速与整体营收增速之间的明显差距，主要来自BD里程碑收入的确认。诺诚健华首席财务官傅欣在27日召开的业绩说明会上表示，扣除药品销售收入后的其余营业收入，主要是公司与Zenas达成的独家许可协议所实现的里程碑收入。回溯来看，2025年10月，诺诚健华子公司InnoCare US与Zenas签署授权协议，将奥布替尼、IL-17抑制剂和TYK2抑制剂在协议约定区域内的相关权益授予Zenas。2026年以来，相关交易对价陆续兑现：上半年公司已确认与IL-17抑制剂对外许可首付款相关收入；8月，InnoCare US又达成与奥布替尼相关的近期里程碑，有权获得Zenas 200万股普通股及2500万美元现金。在此背景下，BD收入对当期营收形成明显推升，而药品销售能否在覆盖相关费用后独立支撑持续盈利，仍是市场关注的核心问题。前三季度研发、销售、管理费用分别为7.85亿元、4.23亿元、1.64亿元，三项费用合计约13.72亿元，规模和同期药品销售收入14.49亿元接近，这也意味着，在剔除BD收入后，诺诚健华内生商业化盈利压力不小。傅欣对此进一步表示，公司2026年第三季度实现持续盈利，2026年1—9月与上年同期相比扭亏为盈。但从目前收入结构来看，BD收入对公司业绩增长形成了较为明显的支撑，药品销售能否在覆盖相关费用后持续支撑盈利，仍待后续观察。二、奥布替尼贡献超九成商业化收入药品销售收入持续增长的背后，是诺诚健华对于奥布替尼这一核心产品的依赖。 title: FDA unveils guidance for ‘plug and play’ gene therapies
content: An article from Dive Brief // Gene editing FDA unveils guidance for ‘plug and play’ gene therapies The plan builds on recent FDA moves to speed “personalized” treatments by offering an approval framework for therapies benefiting different subsets of patients with the same disease. Published Oct. 28, 2026 By Kristin Jensen Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Food and Drug Administration Acting Commissioner Kyle Diamantas delivers remarks during an event at HHS Headquarters August 10, 2026 in Washington, DC. Win McNamee / Staff via Getty Images Dive Brief: The Food and Drug Administration on Tuesday took another step toward expanding access to treatments for rare diseases, announcing a new proposal for personalized gene therapies. In the latest draft guidance, regulators focused on treatments designed to correct different mutations in the same disease-causing gene. Often, the individual mutations are so rare that traditional clinical trials are impractical or even impossible. Under the plan, a drugmaker could win approval for a specific personalized gene therapy targeting one mutation using more of a traditional approach, then later win clearance for different mutations with laboratory data instead of a whole new clinical study. But most people with rare diseases face the stark fact that developing individual treatments requiring clinical studies just isn’t profitable for drugmakers. With the latest plan, the FDA is hoping to change the economic calculus, allowing what TD Cowen analyst Joseph Thome called a “plug and play” optionality. If enacted, this draft guidance could be especially relevant for products under development by gene editing specialist Prime Medicine, Thome wrote in a note to clients. Prime shares jumped 15% early Wednesday. Beam Therapeutics CEO John Evans says the idea would help his company too. “All of this is completely supported by the science of base editing,” Evans wrote in a series of posts on the social media platform X, referring to Beam’s core drug development technology. “But it’s still exhilarating to see the FDA crafting such a forward-looking approach.” Beam’s shares rose 8%. The idea is part of a larger effort by the FDA to encourage drugmakers to develop treatments for rare diseases. The agency is holding a meeting Wednesday afternoon on its White Oak campus to discuss its “Rare Disease Framework Initiative,” which aims to set standards for individual conditions rather than the standard one-size-fits-all approach. Agency officials also attended a rare disease summit in Washington this week. “Senior policymakers are clearly supportive of rare disease,” RBC Capital Markets analyst Luca Issi wrote in a note to clients about the summit. Issi sees a contrast with the “darker days” when former FDA officials Marty Makary and Vinay Prasad left drugmakers frustrated and confused by a series of hard-line stances on therapies even as they unveiled proposals designed to help speed products to market. As part of the administration’s rare disease efforts, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services is also looking to broaden a program that gives Medicaid patients access to cell and gene therapies. Initially, the focus was on sickle cell disease. A big question for developers of gene-editing medicines has been whether one-time prices would become a “roadblock,” Beam’s Evans wrote on X. “Or would payers work to ensure access for patients and capture the long-term benefits of eliminating lifelong medical expenses and chronic treatments?” The CMS plan to expand its access program is “great news,” he said. title: Corxel, an obesity drugmaker, to go public via SPAC deal
content: An article from Dive Brief // Obesity drugs Corxel, an obesity drugmaker, to go public via SPAC deal Armed with a $300 million financing and two GLP-1 and amylin-targeting medicines, Corxel is set to become the latest weight loss-focused company to join the public markets. Published Oct. 26, 2026 Gwendolyn Wu Senior Reporter Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Corxel U.S. will go public via a merger with the SPAC Amanat Acquisition Corp., the companies announced Oct. 26, 2026. Michael Santiago/Getty Images via Getty Images Dive Brief: Corxel Pharmaceuticals, a drug startup developing a pair of weight loss medicines, announced Monday plans to go public by merging with a special purpose acquisition company. The SPAC deal and concurrent $300 million private investment will help Corxel take CX11, a GLP-1 pill licensed from the Chinese drug developer Vincentage Pharma, into late-stage testing. In June, Corxel said CX11 helped participants in a U.S. Phase 2 trial lose an average of up to 11.5% of their body weight after 36 weeks while displaying a “favorable” gastrointestinal tolerability profile. The combined company will also advance a preclinical weight loss prospect directed at a different gut hormone known as amylin. A third drug licensed from Biogen and in development for acute ischemic stroke isn't part of the deal and will instead be housed in a parent entity. Corxel's backers made clear in subsequent talks that they wanted the company to have a "more dedicated focus," rather than pursue "two different tracks," said Kevin Xie, its chief financial officer, in an interview with BioPharma Dive. What followed was a split, with two obesity drugs being merged into a publicly traded entity and the rest of Corxel funneled into a still-private parent. “Both companies have separate development strategies and financing processes, so that’s more welcome news to the investors,” Xie said. Formerly known as Ji Xing Pharmaceuticals, Corxel launched in 2019 and once planned to develop a nasal spray for dry eye disease. It offloaded that therapy in 2024, the same year it acquired from Biogen most rights to JX10 and licensed CX11 from Vincentage. CX11 was already in human testing when Corxel struck that deal. Now it’s on the verge of a global late-stage study. Corxel reported positive late-stage data in May from a Chinese trial run by Vincentage. An international Phase 3 test could follow as soon as the first quarter of 2027. Corxel is pitching CX11 as a “differentiated, next-generation” therapy and an option for people who don’t stay on injectable GLP-1s. Though it is well behind first-to-market oral GLP-1s like Eli Lilly’s Foundayo and Novo’s Wegovy pill, Xie said CX11 may be appealing to people who need to lose 5% to 10% of their body weight and are classified as overweight, but not obese. (Around 31% of U.S. adults fit this description, according to one National Institutes of Health estimate.) Corxel is testing higher doses of CX11 in a Phase 1b trial in an effort to explore the drug’s “efficacy upside,” according to a statement. Additional data are expected in the first half of 2027.
